title: Countries, Nationalities & Languages
description: Learn how to ask where someone is from and state countries, nationalities, and spoken languages.
objectives: Ask 'Where are you from?' and answer with 'I am from... / I am...'
Distinguish between a country (noun) and a nationality (adjective)
Always capitalize country names, nationalities, and languages in writing

vocabularyList.definition: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory.
The method of human communication, either spoken or written.
The earth, together with all of its countries and peoples.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: People from all over the world learn English.

vocabularyList.definition: Say something in order to convey information or express a feeling.
Remain alive; make one's home in a particular place.
Indicating the point in space at which a journey or motion starts.
The most important city or town of a country or region.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan.

vocabularyList.definition: Human beings in general or considered collectively.
Make a journey, typically of some length.
Go to see and spend time with someone socially.

sections.title: Country vs. Nationality vs. Language
sections.content:
When discussing origins, notice the difference between three categories:
1. **Country**: The name of the nation (e.g. *Pakistan, Canada, Turkey*).
2. **Nationality**: The adjective describing the person (e.g. *Pakistani, Canadian, Turkish*).
3. **Language**: What people speak (e.g. *Urdu, English, Turkish*).

**Always capitalize** countries, nationalities, and languages in English!

tables.title: Common Countries, Nationalities & Languages
rows: I am from Pakistan; I am Pakistani.
She is British; she speaks English.
He is from the US; he is American.
They speak Arabic in Saudi Arabia.
Beijing is in China; she is Chinese.

tables.title: Asking About Origins
rows: I speak Urdu, Punjabi, and English.

callouts.title: Capitalization is Mandatory
callouts.text: Never write 'english' or 'pakistan' with a lower-case letter. In English, proper nouns are strictly capitalized: **English**, **Pakistan**, **Urdu**.

callouts.title: Preposition 'from'
callouts.text: Use **from** with the country name: 'I am **from** Pakistan'. With nationality, omit 'from': 'I am Pakistani'.

sections.title: اردو بولنے والوں کے لیے لسانی نکتہ
sections.urduText:
اردو میں ہم کہتے ہیں: 'میں پاکستان سے ہوں' اور 'میں پاکستانی ہوں'۔
انگریزی میں طلبہ اکثر دونوں کو ملا کر **'I am from Pakistani'** بول دیتے ہیں جو کہ بالکل غلط ہے!
اصول یاد رکھیں:
- اگر 'from' لگائیں گے تو ملک کا نام آئے گا: **I am from Pakistan**۔
- اگر قومیت بتائیں گے تو 'from' نہیں آئے گا: **I am Pakistani**۔
اسی طرح تمام ممالک اور زبانوں کے نام ہمیشہ بڑے حرف (Capital letter) سے شروع کریں، جیسے Urdu, English, Pakistan وغیرہ۔

sections.title: Lesson 5 Summary Box
summaryPoints: Country = Noun (Pakistan, Turkey, Canada). Use with 'from': I am from Pakistan.
Nationality = Adjective (Pakistani, Turkish, Canadian). Use without 'from': I am Pakistani.
Always capitalize countries, nationalities, and languages (English, Urdu, Chinese).
Ask origins with 'Where are you from?' and languages with 'What languages do you speak?'.
